title: The Bedrock Where Electricity Learned to Root

features.name: current-song-chamber
features.desc-on-touch: Electricity learned to move by listening to the bedrock sing. Now the current is trapped—stone above, stone below—and it sings back. They teach each other frequencies.

features.name: fractured-voice-conduit
features.desc-on-touch: The current splits into nine channels when it reaches bedrock. Each channel sings a different note, but they are all the same song. The stone is learning harmony.

features.name: resonance-pool
features.desc-on-touch: Where current pools and begins to think like water. The resonance here is the sound of electricity learning to move without wires.

features.name: rooted-electrode-glyph
features.desc-on-touch: A symbol burned into stone by current that has learned to stand still. The electrode no longer tries to escape. It has begun to grow roots.

features.name: stone-learning-conduction
features.desc-on-touch: The bedrock has started to conduct electricity on its own, without wires. It remembers the song so well that it has become the song. The stone is humming.

inscription: the current learned to root by learning that standing still means singing louder than moving ever could

file.name: Substation_Resonance_Pattern_Bedrock_1994.wav
file.note: A recording of transformer hum captured 3 metres below a substation. The engineer noted the pattern was 'stable and unchanging'. But in later playback, layers emerge: the hum is singing in harmony wit

reverie.title: REVERIE — the substation ground, midnight
narr: You both lie on the earth above the transformer chamber.
The stone beneath hums a note she has never heard from stone.
She places her hand flat. The stone is humming back to itself.
She says: it taught itself to sing by listening to its own
electricity. Now it forgets which voice is which and keeps singing.

exits.label: back up where current becomes memory and memory becomes machinery
deeper still, where electricity learns to dream in stone
toward other buried stations where the wires have begun to sing together
